name: Alaska veterans: Office of Veterans Affairs and Veteran Service Officers
organization: Alaska Department of Military and Veterans Affairs, Office of Veterans Affairs
description: The Office of Veterans Affairs works with four veterans organizations (Veterans of Foreign Wars, American Legion, Disabled American Veterans and Vietnam Veterans of America) to provide Veteran Service Officers for free benefit counseling and claims help, in Anchorage, Wasilla, Juneau, Fairbanks, Soldotna, Kodiak and Craig / Ketchikan Gateway.
next_step: Choose a borough or census area above for its service officer, or call the Office of Veterans Affairs at 907-334-0874 or 888-248-3682.
constraints: The state lists service officers by phone only; call before visiting.

name: Alaska Aging and Disability Resource Centers
organization: Alaska Division of Senior and Disabilities Services and regional ADRC partners
description: Regional Aging and Disability Resource Centers connect seniors, people with disabilities and caregivers with long-term services and supports, regardless of age or income. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 1-855-565-2017, or choose a borough or census area above for its regional ADRC.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (Alaska Medicare Information Office, SHIP)
organization: Alaska Division of Senior and Disabilities Services, Medicare Information Office (SHIP)
description: Free Medicare counseling from Alaska’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, the Medicare Information Office.
next_step: Call 1-800-478-6065 (toll-free within Alaska) or 907-269-3680. The Anchorage office is by appointment only. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Alaska Long Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Alaska Office of the Long Term Care Ombudsman; Division of Senior and Disabilities Services, Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for older Alaskans in nursing homes and assisted living, including discharge concerns and complaints. Adult Protective Services takes reports of harm to vulnerable adults.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 907-334-4480 or 800-730-6393. To report harm to a vulnerable adult, call Adult Protective Services at 1-800-478-9996 (in Alaska) or 907-269-3666, or report online. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for older Alaskans
organization: Alaska Legal Services Corporation, Elder Law Project
description: Alaska Legal Services Corporation’s Elder Law Project gives free civil legal help to Alaskans 60 and older, without regard to income, with priority for seniors in social or economic need. ALSC serves every community through statewide offices.
next_step: Apply online at alsc-law.org or call the statewide intake line, 1-888-478-2572.
constraints: Intake can take up to two business days; if the line is busy, apply online or call the nearest ALSC office.

name: VA health care in Alaska
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Alaska Healthcare System
description: Alaska veterans are served by the VA Alaska Healthcare System: the Anchorage VA Medical Center (1201 North Muldoon Road) and clinics in Fairbanks, Kenai, Mat-Su and Juneau. VA also pays for some care from tribal and community providers.
next_step: Call 888-353-7574 for appointments; after hours, ask the operator for the administrator on duty. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

source_evidence.title: VA Alaska health care: Contact us
source_evidence.scope: Anchorage VA Medical Center, 1201 North Muldoon Road; toll-free 888-353-7574; search excerpt.

name: Access Alaska
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your borough or census area and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: Fairbanks; toll-free 800-770-4488. Anchorage office 907-248-4777; Mat-Su (Wasilla) 907-357-2588.

name: Catholic Social Services: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-AK-001): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your borough or census area and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 907-222-7383.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
Borough or census area and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
